newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-IAMA to rectify Primac bid after court ruling.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-IAMA to rectify Primac bid after court ruling.

text.p: The Queensland Supreme Court ruled on Tuesday a takeover document lodged by rural services group IAMA Ltd did not contain enough information for shareholders of its target Primac Holdings Ltd to make an informed decision.
"The judgement was that the Part A did not comply with the Corporations Law," Primac managing director Steve Morrow said.

However, IAMA said it would rectify its Part A offer in the light of the court's judgement. Primac, which recommends rejection of the all-share offer from IAMA, applied to the court last month to restrain despatch of IAMA's Part A document. Primac also sought a declaration that IAMA's Part A did not comply with requirements of the Corporations Law.

The judge ruled the Part A did not comply with the Corporations Law because it made inadequate disclosure concerning relative earnings capacities and of the impact of the offer on IAMA, Morrow said in a statement.
IAMA managing director David Smith said IAMA would take immediate steps to satisfy the requirements set out in the court's judgement.

"It is our objective to put IAMA's offer to all Primac shareholders as soon as possible, thus allowing those shareholders to make a judgement on the reasonableness of the offer," he said in a statement.
IAMA is offering nine of its shares for every 10 Primac.
The Primac board repeated its recommendation that shareholders to reject the offer.
